property_summary: For any caller who has deposited >0, after withdrawAll the contract's ether balance decreases by exactly that depositor's recorded credit (i.e., address(c).balance == initialBalance - creditedAmount); the mutant that sends 0 wei breaks this because the contract balance does not decrease while the credit is cleared.

After any caller deposits some ETH, calling withdrawAll always transfers exactly that caller's recorded credit and reduces contract balance by the same amount; the mutant instead may transfer the entire remaining contract balance (not the caller's credit), breaking this invariant for some inputs.

For any caller who has deposited X > 0, calling withdrawAll always reduces the contract balance by exactly X and leaves the contract balance equal to address(c).balance == initial_balance - X; the mutant can instead send more (the whole remaining balance) causing address(c).balance to decrease by more than the caller's recorded credit for some deposits.

For any caller with a positive recorded credit, calling withdrawAll transfers exactly that caller's recorded credit (so the contract's balance decreases by that same amount); the mutant instead may transfer the entire remaining contract balance causing the contract balance to decrease by more than the caller's recorded credit for some inputs.

For any caller who has positive credit and when another address has also deposited funds into the contract, calling withdrawAll only sends at most the caller's recorded credit (so address(c).balance decreases by <= caller's recorded credit); the mutant can send the entire contract balance when others have deposited, causing address(c).balance to decrease by more than the caller's credit.

After a caller with positive credit calls withdrawAll, the contract's balance decreases by exactly that caller's recorded credit (address(c).balance is reduced by the caller's credit); the mutant can instead send more (the whole remaining balance) and thus violate this equality for some deposits.

After any successful withdrawAll call, the contract's stored balance must equal the contract's actual ETH balance (address(c).balance == c.balance()), but the mutant that decrements balance after the external call can be disrupted by a reentrant attacker causing these to diverge.

For any caller and deposit amount, after withdrawAll completes the contract's stored balance equals its on-chain ETH balance; the mutant that decrements balance after the external call can be re-entered to make these differ.

For any depositor and deposit amount, after calling withdrawAll the contract's recorded internal balance equals its actual ETH balance; moving the internal balance decrement until after the external call allows a reentrant attacker to withdraw twice and make the stored balance exceed the on-chain balance, violating the rule.

For any depositor and deposit amount, if a reentrant attacker calls withdrawAll during its external call, the correct contract C will always end with its internal recorded balance equal to its on-chain ETH balance, while the mutant (which subtracts internal balance after the external call) can be re-entered to make the internal recorded balance differ from the on-chain balance.

For any depositor and any withdrawer, after withdrawAll finishes the contract's internal recorded balance equals its on-chain ETH balance; the mutant that moves the internal balance decrement after the external call can be re-entered to make these differ.

Invariant: after withdrawAll() completes, the caller's credit is zero (the reference always zeros the caller's credit before the external call); the mutant that delays zeroing allows a reentrant caller to observe nonzero credit after completion and thus can break this rule.

For any caller and amount, after withdrawAll() returns the caller's credit getter is zero in the reference (no reentrancy can restore it), but the mutant that delays zeroing allows a reentrant attacker to end a call with a nonzero credit for some inputs.

For any caller and deposit amount, after withdrawAll() completes the caller's recorded credit is zero (the reference zeroes credit before external calls); the mutant that delays zeroing can allow a reentrant attacker to finish withdrawAll with a nonzero stored credit for some inputs.

For any caller and deposit amount, after withdrawAll() returns the caller's recorded credit is zero (reference clears credit before external call); the mutant that defers zeroing can allow a reentrant attacker to finish withdrawAll with a nonzero stored credit for some inputs.

For any caller and deposit amount, after withdrawAll() completes the caller's credit (the public mapping getter) is zero in the correct contract; the mutant that delays zeroing can allow a reentrant attacker to finish withdrawAll with a nonzero recorded credit for some inputs.

Invariant: calling withdrawAll always preserves that when a depositor had positive credit, after withdrawAll completes their recorded credit becomes 0 (the reference always clears credit[msg.sender] to 0 even if the external call fails; the mutant can leave credit nonzero when the external call fails but balance stayed non-negative).

For any caller and deposit amount, after calling withdrawAll the reference C always sets credit[caller] to 0 regardless of whether the external transfer to the caller fails, but the mutant can leave credit[caller] nonzero when the external call fails yet balance remained non-negative.

For any caller and deposited amount, after withdrawAll returns the contract's recorded credit for that caller is zero in the correct C implementation (it clears credit[msg.sender] unconditionally), whereas the mutant can leave the caller's credit nonzero when the external transfer to the caller fails but balance remained non-negative (because it conditionally requires the call result instead of always reverting on failed send).

For any depositor and deposit amount, calling withdrawAll on the reference C either successfully sends the depositor their credit and leaves contract balance decreased accordingly, or (if the external call reverts) the whole withdrawAll call reverts; the mutant can swallow a failing external call when internal balance stays non-negative, causing withdrawAll to return (not revert) despite the external transfer failing — observable as address(c).balance remaining higher than expected while credit was cleared.

For any depositor and deposit amount, if the depositor's external fallback call fails during withdrawAll, the correct contract always reverts the withdrawAll (so the call does not return successfully), whereas the mutant can return successfully when balance remains non-negative and thus swallow the failing external call.
